result.text:
Done — 57 tests pass (the original 16 plus 41 new ones).

## Design

**Commands as objects** (`CrawlerCommand` hierarchy). `process` still interprets character by character, so outside a guarded run the commands before a bad one are executed, as in v1. `CrawlerCommand.commandFor(char)` maps a character to a command via a polymorphic `isFor(char)` lookup (same idiom as `CrawlerFacing.facing`):
- `CrawlerMovement` (advance / retreat / turn cw / turn ccw) are the only ones that know how to be **repeated** and that answer an `inverse()` for undoing.
- `RepeatLastCommand` is what a digit creates: it repeats the last command `digit + 2` more times, so `"a0"` advances 3 times. Since only movements accept repetition, a digit after `(`, `)` or another digit is an invalid command.
- `InvalidCommand` is the null object used both for unknown characters and for "the command before the first one" — that's what makes a leading digit invalid, with no special-casing.

**Ground decides the movement** (`SeabedGround` hierarchy + `Sonar`). The crawler asks the sonar for the ground of the position a command ends at and the ground answers the resulting position: `FirmSand` the expected one, `Silt` the one after sliding 1..10 cells (`SlideDistance`, random by default, fixed in tests), `Boulder` signals. Turning asks the ground the crawler stands on to `turn(aCrawlerTurn)`: `TraversableGround` performs it, `Boulder` signals — which is exactly why silt doesn't affect turning. `SurveyCrawler.atFacing(...)` still works because it defaults to a `FirmSandSonar`.

**Guarded run as a state** (`CrawlerRun`: `NormalRun` / `GuardedRun`). The state decides which movements are predictable (guarded runs ask for `predictablePositionAfterMovingFrom`, which silt refuses), which movements are remembered, and what `(`, `)` and the end of the sequence mean. `process` catches any error, tells the failed run to undo itself — the inverse of each registered movement in reverse order, so the crawler physically walks back and restores its facing — and re-signals the error.

## Test cases beyond the statement
Digit not remembered across `process` calls; `"a00"` (only one digit); digit after `(` or `)`; crawler keeps working after a boulder error and after a failed guarded run; turning while standing on a boulder (also inside a guarded run, where there is nothing to undo); silt when retreating slides backwards; random silt over 1000 runs reaches exactly the 10 possible positions; only the failing guarded run is undone (`"(aa)(aa)"`); commands before and after a guarded run are kept; repeated commands inside a guarded run are undone; `)` without `(`.

The README has a new section documenting all of this.
